key_insight: SILSA replaces fragmented local 3D token generation with compact sliding-window slice latents, helping preserve surface topology while still supporting high-resolution shape synthesis. The result is a more coherent and efficient way to generate thin, connected, and detail-rich 3D objects.
problem_solved: High-resolution 3D generation often uses multi-stage voxel pipelines that split shapes into many local tokens, increasing compute cost and making it easy to break thin structures or complex topologies. This paper addresses the need for a topology-preserving representation that keeps surfaces continuous.
method: Represents 3D shapes using compact sliding-window slice latents instead of many fragmented local tokens.
Uses a topology-aware generation framework designed to maintain connectivity and continuity across slices.
Supports high-resolution synthesis while reducing generation overhead and improving consistency for challenging shapes.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, SILSA offers a more scalable and topology-aware alternative to standard voxel-based 3D generation pipelines. It is especially useful for applications where preserving thin structures, holes, and connected surfaces is critical.

paper_title: SILSA: Sliding-Window Slice Latents for Topology-Preserving High-Resolution 3D Generation
paper_authors: Tianjiao Yu, Xinzhuo Li, Yifan Shen, Ying Shen, Kiet A. Nguyen
